close_reason: parse_ws_frame restructured to call serde_json::from_str directly against the original text for typed branches, keeping the parsed Value alive for the Unknown fallback. Eliminates the unconditional deep Value.clone() on every successful StateChange/Response frame. Existing degradation tests pass.
description: src/ws/mod.rs:161-175 — for both StateChange and Response branches: `let raw = val.clone(); match serde_json::from_value::<T>(val) { Ok(...) => ..., Err(_) => Ok(WsFrame::Unknown { type_name, raw }) }`. The clone happens unconditionally — even when the deserialize succeeds and `raw` is discarded. For 1-MiB-cap WS messages this allocates and drops a non-trivial copy on every successful frame, in a hot path (every push notification). Idiomatic Rust alternative: try the typed deserialize first against `&val` (Value implements Deserializer by reference for owned-form deserialization is more involved, but `serde_json::from_value` consumes Value — use `serde_path_to_error` style or restructure). Cheaper option: compute typed deserialize via `serde_json::from_value::<StateChange>(val.clone())` only on the error branch — but that's the same cost. Best fix: deserialize from the original text directly using `serde_json::from_str::<TaggedFrame>(text)` where TaggedFrame is an enum with #[serde(tag = "@type")]. Eliminates the Value intermediate and the clone. Note: locked crate.
title: parse_ws_frame clones the full Value before every typed deserialize
